messages:
alex: Heads-up — running into a weird edge with the Kotlin client + OkHttp. After adding our AuthInterceptor and the retry interceptor, outgoing requests sometimes have two Authorization headers. Seen this before?
mira: Hmm. Did you add the auth header in both the interceptor and manually on the Request.Builder?
alex: No, interceptor only. Minimal repro: interceptor attaches header, then OkHttp retry (when 503) replays request and we end up with header duplicated. Code: ```kotlin class AuthInterceptor: Interceptor { override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response { val req = chain.request().newBuilder().addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer ${token}").build() return chain.proceed(req) } } ```
ryan: Ok. Two quick guesses: 1) The token string already has `Authorization:` prefix (rare) or 2) some other interceptor does `.header()` vs `.addHeader()` semantics on retry causing duplication.
sophie: Also check whether you mutate the original request vs building a new one — OkHttp caches header fields differently on retries if the request has a body that isn't replayable.
alex: Good point. We're using `.addHeader()` — should maybe use `.header()` to replace any existing?
mira: `.header()` replaces existing header name; `.addHeader()` appends. If you want single header always, use `.header("Authorization", "Bearer ...")`. But be careful if some other layer expects multiple headers (unlikely for auth).
ryan: Another angle: our client shading could be causing two different Interceptor classes to be present on classpath in certain apps (one from the shaded jar, one from unshaded dependency) — leading to the interceptor executing twice.
sophie: Ah right — shading pitfalls. If host app bundles OkHttp or the SDK shaded okhttp version collides, you can get duplicate execution. Check the final artifact (fat JAR or Android apk) for two okhttp versions.
alex: How can I quickly verify?
mira: Run `./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` or use `jar tvf build/libs/sdk-all.jar | grep okhttp` to see duplicates.
ryan: Also check proguard/R8 mappings on Android — shading + relocation rules can accidentally keep both.
alex: Thanks. One other issue while debugging: streaming completions stream back NDJSON lines but our Jackson deserializer chokes on trailing commas when using object mapper configured with both Gson and Jackson on classpath (we shade gson). Any tips?
sophie: If you have both Gson and Jackson on classpath and some libs call `ServiceLoader` or pick default mappers, behavior can be inconsistent. For NDJSON, best is to parse line-by-line with a streaming parser: Jackson `JsonFactory` + `JsonParser` for each line, or use Gson's `JsonReader` per line.
ryan: Example small snippet: ```kotlin val reader = BufferedReader(response.body!!.charStream()) reader.lineSequence().forEach { line -> if (line.isBlank()) return@forEach val node = jacksonMapper.readTree(line) // handle node } ```
mira: Also ensure your okhttp `ResponseBody` `charStream()`/`source()` isn't consumed twice by a debug interceptor. That can corrupt streaming.
alex: Good call. One more: we have a shading relocation for `com.fasterxml.jackson` to `io.redwood.shaded.jackson`. But tests on CI show NoClassDefFoundError for `com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonFactory` in some modules. Any causes?
sophie: That usually means the module that expects unshaded name is loading a Jackson class via reflection (e.g., ServiceLoader) and the relocation didn't update the reflective lookup. Relocation needs to include `META-INF/services` entries or you must add `relocate` rules for service files.
ryan: Yep, with shadow plugin use `relocate('com.fasterxml', 'io.redwood.shaded.fasterxml')` and `transform(com.github.jengelman.gradle.plugins.shadow.transformers.ServiceFileTransformer)` to merge and rewrite service files.
mira: CI trick: run the JVM with `-verbose:class` for the failing class to see which jar provides it.
alex: This is gold — I'll try replacing `.addHeader()` with `.header()` and inspect the shaded jars + services merge. If that doesn't fix duplication, I will dump dependency tree and paste here. Thanks! :thumbsup:
ci-bot: deploy-status: CI pipeline for alex/sdk-kotlin #238 finished — tests passed on linux but one integration flaky on macos (streaming). :robot_face:
alex: Noted — will run the macos streaming integration locally. Ping me if you spot anything else.
mira: If you need a quick code review after the header change I can look.
sophie: And if you hit reflection/service loader issues, @ryan can share our shadow config that worked for dedicated infra.
ryan: I'll paste our working `shadowJar` snippet later.
alex: Great, thanks everyone.
